tweets: A malicious contract can take over control flow and call back before your function finishes.
This allows different invocations to interact in ways that cause undesirable outcomes.
The root cause is updating internal state after an external call executes.
Best practice: perform all internal state changes before making any external calls.
Using a reentrancy lock helps avoid this weakness by blocking unwanted callbacks.
Follow the Checks-Effects-Interactions pattern to maintain safe execution order.
